events.title: Gandhi Begins the Salt March
events.description: Mahatma Gandhi set out from his ashram near Ahmedabad on a roughly 240-mile march to the Arabian Sea at Dandi. He led it in defiance of the British monopoly on salt. Thousands of followers joined him along the way.
events.significance: The march turned a simple household staple into a symbol of resistance. It energized India's independence movement and drew worldwide attention to nonviolent protest.

events.title: German Troops Enter Austria
events.description: German forces crossed the border into Austria, and the annexation known as the Anschluss was declared the following day. The takeover was carried out with almost no armed resistance.
events.significance: It was Nazi Germany's first major territorial expansion by force or threat of force. It showed that the European powers would not stop Hitler's aggression, and it set the stage for the crises that led to World War II.

events.title: Juliette Gordon Low Founds the Girl Guides in the U.S.
events.description: In Savannah, Georgia, Juliette Gordon Low gathered a small group of girls for the first meeting of an organization that was later renamed the Girl Scouts of the USA. The girls took part in outdoor activities, learned practical skills and did community service.
events.significance: The organization grew into one of the largest girls' leadership programs in the world. It has shaped generations of women through service, education and independence.

events.title: St. Francis Dam Collapses in California
events.description: Just before midnight, the St. Francis Dam north of Los Angeles failed. A wall of water swept down the Santa Clara River valley and killed roughly 400 people.
events.significance: It was one of the worst civil engineering failures in American history. It led to stricter oversight of dam design and construction and ended the career of its chief engineer, William Mulholland.
